title: Microsoft Teams: enhanced media quality for Direct Guest Join
summary: Hold: the advice to tell users that Google Meet Direct Guest Join is unavailable on Teams Rooms for Android omits Microsoft's September 2026 release announcement. The roadmap still carries that restriction, so the briefing must report the disagreement rather than present it as the current availability rule. The documented background controls and licensing statements otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Administrators should tell users Google Meet through DGJ is not yet available on Teams Rooms for Android, per the roadmap.
claims.quote:
1449/1.0.96.2026261804 (September 2026)
Introduced in this update:
1. Google Meet for Direct Guest Join: Organizations now have expanded meeting interoperability with two-way Direct Guest Join (DGJ) between Google Meet and Microsoft Teams meetings.
claims.fix: Replace the Android availability statements and the rollout instruction with: 'The roadmap still says Google Meet DGJ is not yet available on Teams Rooms for Android, but Learn's September 2026 Android release notes announce two-way Google Meet DGJ in version 1449/1.0.96.2026261804. Report this discrepancy to room users rather than asserting unavailability.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-release-note#teams-rooms-on-android-feature-introduction-and-issue-resolution. Remove the open question asking when it will reach Android.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: Review is the action rating for this launched improvement to existing DGJ meeting media.
claims.quote: action: "review"; 'treat them as arriving with DGJ rather than as something you switch on.' The standard assigns prepare to an arriving redesign or replacement of existing behaviour, including when its default is unknown.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': this is an improvement arriving in existing DGJ meetings, not a capability that changes nothing until an administrator chooses it.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells readers to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: 'Ask the network team to confirm that firewalls and web filters allow the rooms to reach each provider's website without authentication, with the right QoS class'; table rows cover provider toggles, calendar processing and a tenant-switch gap.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet that asks the network team to confirm firewall, web-filter and QoS controls; those controls have no table row. Retain the existing background explanation of the network prerequisites.

claims.claim: WebRTC is a browser-style real-time media technology.
claims.quote: The WebRTC API is a web standard that enables real-time communication (RTC) between browsers and mobile applications.
claims.fix: Remove the explanatory clause 'a browser-style real-time media technology' to avoid adding a source about an unrelated product solely for this definition.

claims.claim: Learn instructs administrators to ensure tenant policies do not block devices from third-party meeting services.
claims.quote: Ensure no tenant policies are blocking devices from connecting to third-party meeting services.
